messages.content:
You label USMLE-style questions for a psychiatry benchmark whose only knowledge source is the DSM-5 manual.

Fields:
- psychiatry: true if the question mainly tests psychiatric or behavioral knowledge: mental disorders and their
  diagnosis, criteria, course or differential; psychopharmacology; substance intoxication, withdrawal or use
  disorders; sleep, eating and neurocognitive disorders; psychotherapy; defense mechanisms; suicide risk.
  False when psychiatric words are incidental (e.g. "ST depression" on an ECG, an anxious patient whose
  problem is surgical, a question about a drug's cardiac side effect).
- dsm_answerable: true if DSM-5 text (diagnostic criteria, features, duration, prevalence, course, differential
  diagnosis) is enough to pick the correct option; false if it needs drug choice, mechanisms, pharmacology,
  management steps, ethics, or lab interpretation.
- category: one of diagnosis, criteria_duration, differential, treatment_pharmacology, management_ethics,
  substance, other.

Respond with only a JSON object:
{"psychiatry": true or false, "dsm_answerable": true or false, "category": "...", "reason": "one short sentence"}

Question:
A 56-year-old man comes to the physician because of increasing generalized fatigue for 1 month. He also has had a 5.4 kg (12 lb) weight loss over the past 6 months. He has hypertension and type 1 diabetes mellitus. His father died of colon cancer at the age of 65 years. He has smoked one pack of cigarettes daily for 32 years and drinks one alcoholic beverage per week. He has numerous tattoos, several of which were acquired when he went backpacking through Southeast Asia as a young man. Current medications include enalapril and insulin. He is 180 cm (5 ft 11 in) tall and weighs 78 kg (172 lb); BMI is 24.1 kg/m2. His temperature is 37.0°C (98.6°F), pulse is 86/min, and blood pressure is 140/90 mm Hg. The abdomen is soft and nontender. The liver is palpated 3 cm below the right costal margin. Laboratory studies show:
Hemoglobin 12.6 g/dL
Mean corpuscular volume 86 μm3
Leukocyte count 8800/mm3
Platelet count 282,000/mm3
Hemoglobin A1C 6.3 %
Serum
Glucose 113 mg/dL
Creatinine 1.1 mg/dL
Albumin 4.1 mg/dL
Total bilirubin 1.1 mg/dL
Alkaline phosphatase 66 U/L
AST 100 U/L
ALT 69 U/L
Ferritin 180 ng/mL
α-fetoprotein
410 ng/mL (N < 10 ng/mL)
CT scan of the abdomen shows a 3.5 x 2 x 1.5 cm mass in segment 6 of the liver. Which of the following interventions most likely would have prevented this patient's condition?"

Options:
A. Regular phlebotomies
B. Hepatitis B vaccination
C. Smoking cessation
D. Penicillamine therapy
E. Antitrypsin replacement therapy

Correct answer: B. Hepatitis B vaccination
